This verdict is independent verification evidence and does not constitute human approval or publication.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Are there pickups, partial bars, meter or key changes?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: No. Common time and the three-flat signature persist. All 41 regions are complete bars; the accompaniment uses the established triplet grouping. No cadenza is printed.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Do the first and second endings and repeat strokes create separate short regions?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: No. P012 and P013 are full alternative endings, each with its bracket. The backward repeat closes P012; the forward repeat opens P014. Each compound repeat is a single boundary.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Does the first ending close at the system break before the second ending?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. P031 ends with a complete backward repeat; P032 is the complete second ending on the next system. There is no split bar. The repeat returns to P014.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Does any last region lack its closing barline?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: No. All system endings have complete closing strokes through both staves. Recount by system: 3, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, 4. No split regions are needed.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Are both later clefs correctly located and musically addressed?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. The treble glyph in P037 follows two beats of accompaniment and governs the next group on beat three. The bass glyph is inside P038 after its final half rest and governs the opening of P039. The treble clef at the start of system 12 reiterates the current clef. No other changes or cautionary clefs are printed.

irregular_checks.question_plain: Is the narrow final region a complete bar with a complete final boundary?
irregular_checks.answer_plain: Yes. Whole notes with fermatas occupy a full common-time bar. The final thin and thick strokes are one closing boundary. Both fermatas and the tied upper notes remain inside the crop.

checklist.question: Do all staves, notes, rests, slurs and other musical marks fit completely inside the page?
On every full-page red crop rectangle, is all tempo text, dynamics, hairpins, slurs, stems, flags, pedal notation, octave lines and other musical ink inside the rectangle?
Do the blue lines match every printed barline, giving 41 printed regions?
Where red geometry and blue Prep boundaries differed, does the final frame follow the printed barlines rather than either proposal automatically?
Do the compact red labels state every visible repeat, ending, route mark, special barline, partial, meter/key change and clef change—and are all unlabeled blue regions truly normal?
Are all region labels outside the printed system, with no ending, repeat, clef, note or mark hidden?
Does the clef list state each opening clef and every visible clef change?
